Package com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.entity

Class BrainEntity

java.lang.Object
com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.entity.Entity
com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.entity.BrainEntity
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.bukkit.event.Listener
Direct Known Subclasses:
HumanoidBrainEntity
public abstract class BrainEntity extends Entity
Abstract base class for custom entities that use the beta MannequinBrain system (sensors + goal selectors) instead of the legacy EntityAI tick approach.

Extend this class (or HumanoidBrainEntity for mannequin-based entities) when you want the structured perception/behavior separation that the brain provides. The legacy DumbEntity hierarchy is left completely untouched — both systems coexist.

Subclass contract:

  1. Override configureBrain(com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.ai.beta.MannequinBrain, org.bukkit.entity.Mannequin) to register your sensors and goals onto the freshly created brain before it starts ticking.
  2. The brain is started automatically at the end of spawn(org.bukkit.Location) after configureBrain(com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.ai.beta.MannequinBrain, org.bukkit.entity.Mannequin) returns.
  3. The brain is shut down automatically when the entity dies (onDeath(org.bukkit.event.entity.EntityDeathEvent)).

Minimal example: 


 public class WanderingMerchantEntity extends BrainEntity {

     public WanderingMerchantEntity(JavaPlugin plugin) {
         super(plugin, "wandering_merchant", EntityType.MANNEQUIN,
               Component.text("Wandering Merchant"));
     }

     {@literal @}Override
     protected void configureBrain(MannequinBrain brain, Mannequin mannequin) {
         brain.getSensorSelector()
              .addSensor(mannequin, new NearestItemSensor(plugin, 8.0, 3));
         brain.getNormalSelector()
              .addGoal(1, new LookAtPlayerGoal());
         brain.getNormalSelector()
              .addGoal(2, new WanderGoal(mannequin.getLocation()));
         brain.getTargetSelector()
              .addGoal(1, new NearestPlayerTargetGoal(plugin));
     }
 }

Note: BrainEntity currently only supports EntityType.MANNEQUIN for the brain, because MannequinBrain is typed to Mannequin. If you spawn a non-mannequin type the brain will not be created and a warning will be logged. Non-mannequin brain support can be added later by generalising the brain to LivingEntity.

  • Method Details

    • spawn

      public org.bukkit.entity.Entity spawn(org.bukkit.Location location)
      Spawns the entity, builds a MannequinBrain for it, calls configureBrain(com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.ai.beta.MannequinBrain, org.bukkit.entity.Mannequin) so subclasses can register sensors and goals, then starts the brain ticking.

      If the spawned entity is not a Mannequin the brain is skipped and a warning is logged — the entity is still returned normally so callers don't have to handle null.

      Overrides:
      spawn in class Entity
      Parameters:
      location - where to spawn the entity
      Returns:
      the spawned Bukkit entity

    • configureBrain

      protected abstract void configureBrain(MannequinBrain brain, org.bukkit.entity.Mannequin mannequin)
      Called during spawn(org.bukkit.Location) after the entity is created but before the brain starts ticking.

      Register all sensors and goals here. The brain has already been constructed; do not call MannequinBrain.start() yourself.

      Parameters:
      brain - the fresh brain for this entity instance
      mannequin - the spawned mannequin the brain controls

    • onDeath

      public void onDeath(org.bukkit.event.entity.EntityDeathEvent event)
      Shuts down the brain for any entity that dies.

      Delegates drop handling to the parent Entity.onDeath(org.bukkit.event.entity.EntityDeathEvent) first, then cleanly shuts down the associated brain (unregisters sensors, stops goals, cancels the tick task).

      Overrides:
      onDeath in class Entity
      Parameters:
      event - The EntityDeathEvent triggered when this entity dies
